html:
The Guatemalan coup of 1954 overthrew President Jacobo Árbenz in June 1954. It was organised by the CIA, in an operation called PBSuccess, and led by the exiled officer Carlos Castillo Armas.

The United States government feared communism in Guatemala and was close to the United Fruit Company, hit by the land reform of Árbenz. The CIA trained a small rebel force in Honduras, bombed Guatemala City with hired pilots and ran a radio station spreading false reports of a large invasion. The army refused to fight, and Árbenz resigned on 27 June.

Castillo Armas undid the land reform and arrested thousands. A young doctor, Che Guevara, was in the city and drew the lesson that a revolution needs its own army. The coup became a model for the Cold War in Latin America and led to decades of military rule.
sum: The Guatemalan coup of 1954 overthrew President Jacobo Árbenz in June 1954. It was organised by the CIA, in an operation called PBSuccess, and led by the exiled officer Carlos Castillo Armas.
